chapter: Advice to youth and the art of drumming
title: College-trained young players and Dave Voruff
summary: Saunders praises youngsters from college bands who played for his date, especially altoist Dave Voruff.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Do you think that the jazz courses in college, like Governors State has a very good band --
Do you think that's improving, the -- raising the level of music?

Right, it is, it's definitely -- I did a job here a couple of weeks ago, and I had the fortunate -- I was fortunate enough to have to hire four trumpet players. Three of the trumpet players were youngsters, just out of school, out of maybe college. It was fantastic, fantastic.

And as I say, these young trumpet players, they were fantastic. And I had a little alto player, and I'll have to find his name here. I'll get it for you in a minute, but he was fantastic. And he reminded me of Bunky Green. He played so good and he just loved it. And he was about Bunky's size and about his age, maybe a little younger.
Yeah. Well, Bunky's got several students.
Well, I didn't ask him. I didn't want to be too facetious, but he -- oh, man, this guy was
Druck. Dave -- Voruff, I'm sorry. V-o-r-u-f-f, Dave. Dave Voruff. Man.

And he'd come in late for rehearsal. He told me he was going to be a few minutes late, because he had a transcription. And it turned out it wasn't a transcription, it was a record date. So it drew him late and he come in late for rehearsal, and he felt so guilty that he -- we had a cocktail hour, it was only about five minutes. He said, let me make it up, let me play.
He came in and played the cocktail hour, the dinner hour and the show and everything else. I mean, terrific.
